policy: Each record keeps independent axes: implementation, local tests, production observation, comparison. Filing a record is not closure. A mismatch closes only after reproduction, an evidence-based expectation, a fix, regression tests and a re-comparison on a new artifact; an unobserved item closes only after a production observation that either matches (evidence attached) or leads to a fix on this branch. Closed records stay in the file.

gaps.scope: An account disabled after its MFA pending credential was issued could complete mfaSignIn:finalize and receive tokens; mfaSignIn:start issued a code for it.
gaps.nextAction: Production error precedence for USER_DISABLED at this endpoint and retention of the pending credential across disable/re-enable are unobserved; observe if a corpus is planned.

gaps.scope: A beforeSignIn response setting disabled: true was applied and tokens were still issued on the same request. Production (recorded, scoped approval) refuses the same request with USER_DISABLED.
gaps.nextAction: Local comparison recorded: the refusal on the same request matches; the immediate readback of the flag differs on one path and is tracked as GAP-AUTH-001.

gaps.scope: Persistence of a hook-applied disable. Production (recorded 2026-09-11 and 2026-09-12): an MFA finalize persists the flag; a sign-up keeps a created, disabled record; a first-factor password sign-in of an existing account persists nothing (false before, immediately after, 5 s and ~31 s after, and 30 s after with no earlier read) while sign-ins stay refused only under the registered function. fireemu persisted on every path; it now persists for sign-up and MFA finalize only.
gaps.nextAction: Closed for the recorded conditions: production candidate and the local comparison on the corrected artifact each carry a scoped approval; other first-factor paths (email link, IdP, custom token, phone) follow the existing-account rule unobserved.

gaps.scope: Enterprise / Native pipeline execution: inputs are decoded and validated, a valid pipeline still returns UNIMPLEMENTED; expression function names and return types are partly unchecked.
gaps.nextAction: Decompose the official pipeline stages and expressions; implement the evaluator, type and error checks and the executor stage by stage with an oracle corpus per stage.

gaps.scope: Enterprise full-text search: text index definitions are validated only; backfill, posting data, search execution and scoring are not implemented.
gaps.nextAction: Implement definition, build state, update tracking and search execution separately, each compared against an oracle.

gaps.scope: Administrative accounts:update of an already disabled account. Production (recorded 2026-09-12): password replacement and photo update are accepted and applied, no tokens are returned, the account's own sign-in stays USER_DISABLED, and the new password signs in after re-enablement. fireemu returned tokens for the password change; fixed so tokens follow a credential change only for an account enabled after the update.
gaps.nextAction: Closed: production candidate and local comparison each carry a scoped approval.

gaps.scope: An account created by the request that a blocking function disables. Production (recorded 2026-09-12, revision 2 with an email-prefix selector): the creating sign-up is refused with USER_DISABLED, the record exists and is disabled, a second sign-up is EMAIL_EXISTS; the local artifact showed the same rows before the run.
gaps.nextAction: Closed for the recorded sign-up path: production candidate and local comparison each carry a scoped approval. Other auto-creating methods stay unobserved.

gaps.scope: MFA finalize refusal precedence. Production (recorded and approved 2026-09-12, auth-refusal-precedence revision 1): a disabled account holding an SMS session is refused INVALID_CODE with a wrong code and USER_DISABLED with the correct code, so the verification code is checked before the account state, and the same held pending credential and session complete after re-enablement, so neither refusal consumes them. fireemu already matched on these rows. The remaining precedence is unobserved: an expired pending credential against a code valid on its own, and mfaSignIn:start on a disabled account.
gaps.nextAction: The observed overlaps match fireemu and are approved through the auth-refusal-precedence receipt; no MFA change is made. The tampered-token accounts:update divergence is tracked separately as GAP-AUTH-003 (AUTH-USERS). Next for AUTH-U03: a later revision observing an expired pending credential against an independently valid code (needs the production pending lifetime, so a separate corpus) and mfaSignIn:start on a disabled account. Do not generalize the observed order to TOTP or expiry.

gaps.scope: Other revocation triggers against an existing pending credential: password change, password reset, administrative password update, provider unlink. Only the explicit validSince update is observed and approved.
gaps.nextAction: The parameterized recorder (tools/auth-pending-triggers) covers all four triggers with offline safety tests and completes on an owned local artifact for each; the held credential survives every trigger locally, which is fireemu's behavior, not evidence of production. Next: a production run per trigger under its own execution approval (temporary MFA and test-phone configuration, restored; provider-unlink links a federated identity administratively as a precondition), then per-trigger publication, comparison and scoped approval. Do not generalize the explicit-validSince result to these triggers.

gaps.scope: Credentials after re-enablement: pending credential, SMS code, used TOTP step and pre-disable refresh token, distinguishing administrative disable from hook disable and from natural expiry.
gaps.nextAction: Local regressions exist for the administrative path; observe in production per credential kind.

gaps.scope: Production lifetimes and boundaries of SMS codes, pending credentials and TOTP windows, including resend behavior and reuse limits. Local VirtualClock tests cover the emulator only.
gaps.nextAction: Observe with waits bounded to the documented lifetimes; record exact-boundary behavior separately.

gaps.scope: TOTP and tenant behavior in production: enrollment conditions, unenrollment, two-party ownership, per-tenant settings and cross-namespace refusal. Local two-party and tenant tests are not production evidence.
gaps.nextAction: Plan TOTP enablement on the oracle (a configuration change) and a tenant corpus.

gaps.scope: Other blocking response fields and events: fields other than disabled, customClaims versus sessionClaims, beforeCreate, explicit rejection, timeout, multiple events. sessionClaims stay non-persistent locally.
gaps.nextAction: One corpus per response shape; keep the disabling-response approval separate.

gaps.scope: Which sign-in methods invoke blocking functions: first IdP sign-in, linking to an existing account, anonymous and custom-token sign-in (documented as not triggering). No uniform expectation across methods.
gaps.nextAction: Check the local handler set against the documentation; observe methods whose documentation is ambiguous.

gaps.scope: Concurrency and changes during a hook: real concurrent requests, deletion, revocation or factor change while the hook runs, sweeps by another adapter, failures after finalization (signing, response). The eight-thread test does not enumerate interleavings.
gaps.nextAction: Split into separately testable cases; local first, production where observable.

gaps.scope: Duplicate email owners and UID reuse: owner switching on user_mut is a local model; production compatibility of owner resolution and of credentials after re-creation is unobserved.
gaps.nextAction: Observe with allowDuplicateEmails where applicable; compare ID and refresh token outcomes separately.

gaps.scope: Password rules on other routes: signUp, reset, administrative update, import; minimum length, normalization, truncation, custom policies. The 4095/4096/4097 approval covers one route and ASCII/astral inputs.
gaps.nextAction: Per-route corpora reusing the maximum-password recorder.

gaps.scope: Production error details for the authorization fixes (lookup identifier search, update administrator-only fields, OOB link return): input types, null and empty values, multiple invalid conditions.
gaps.nextAction: Observe error classes per condition; keep the local authorization fixes.

gaps.scope: Token validity across verification paths: REST lookup and refresh, Admin SDK checkRevoked, Rules, other services, project and tenant boundaries, actual expiry. expiresIn=3600 is not an expiry test.
gaps.nextAction: Design a bounded actual-expiry observation and per-path verification cases.

gaps.scope: REST and gRPC read, write and query surfaces: per-method fields, enums, oneofs, type boundaries; Commit atomicity versus BatchWrite partial results. Broad parity requirements are not per-item evidence.
gaps.nextAction: Map each method to cases and existing tests; list unmapped items.

gaps.scope: Aggregations outside the approved 14 cases: gRPC, SDK and Rules paths, other numeric, index and concurrency conditions.
gaps.nextAction: Attach evidence per path; do not extend the REST approval.

gaps.scope: Transactions and contention: concurrency mode of the real database, retry, timeout, ordering, state and resources after failure.
gaps.nextAction: Observe against production per condition; do not infer mode from the edition.

gaps.scope: Listen and WebChannel: event completeness and order, disconnect, reconnect, resume, interaction with SDK cache and auth switches.
gaps.nextAction: Separate resource-limit tests from semantics; observe production per scenario.

gaps.scope: Rules and indexes: authorization, evaluation budget, invariance after denial, index direction and merging, Standard versus Enterprise differences, reload.
gaps.nextAction: Do not reuse admin-bypass production observations as Rules evidence.

gaps.scope: Administrative API: database and index lifecycle, TTL, backup, restore, PITR, import, export, long-running operations.
gaps.nextAction: Distinguish input acceptance, local state transitions and real cloud operation.

gaps.scope: MongoDB compatibility: inventory of APIs, types and drivers, and per-item implementation and test status.
gaps.nextAction: Inventory first; do not transfer Native evidence.

gaps.scope: SDKs and platforms: Web and Node clients, Admin, mobile; lockfile binding, offline cache, pending writes, listeners with Auth handoff. Declared dependencies are not execution evidence.
gaps.nextAction: Per-SDK execution receipts bound to lockfiles.

gaps.scope: Denominator of the official specification: URL enumeration, fetch, section extraction and semantic review are separate steps; the 2026-09-09 snapshot count is not coverage.
gaps.nextAction: Keep the acquisition steps separate in the inventory pages.

gaps.scope: Decomposition into atomic requirements: API and field enumerations are not yet connected to per-condition requirements and cases; unmapped is not unsupported.
gaps.nextAction: Extend the requirement ledger per surface.

gaps.scope: Re-comparison on the current artifact: preserved historical receipts do not show the latest binary passes the same cases.
gaps.nextAction: Run current corpora in priority order with recorded source, profile and configuration.

gaps.scope: Local side of production-only receipts: every production candidate or approved record is paired with a local run of the same corpus and a published comparison record. As of 2026-09-12 all five corpora (blocking disable, pending revocation, readback timing, revision 2 created-then-disabled, disabled-account administrative update) have comparison records bound to their build commits and fixture digests.
gaps.nextAction: Keep pairing future production records with a local comparison; results are tracked per corpus.

On the artifact recorded at the time (comparison record at commit 98be375, kept in history), the immediate readback of the flag for the password-sign-in account read true locally and false in production while the other eleven rows agreed. The current comparison record, regenerated from a run on the corrected artifact with fixture digests, agrees on all twelve rows; the correction is the one made under GAP-AUTH-001.
gaps.nextAction: Closed: the corrected comparison carries a scoped approval; the original mismatch stays in history at commit 98be375.

gaps.scope: Comparison result of the pending-revocation corpus: all eight rows agree in scope between the owned local artifact and the approved production record.
gaps.nextAction: None; other revocation triggers stay under AUTH-U04.

gaps.scope: A public source of truth for open work: GitHub issues were empty and private issues are not visible; this ledger is the public record and keeps closed history.
gaps.nextAction: Keep this file current; do not treat filing alone as closure.

gaps.scope: accounts:signUp and photoUrl: the REST reference lists the field, but production does not persist it (recorded 2026-09-12, control row of tools/auth-blocking-create-disable revision 1: absent on lookup, invisible to a blocking hook). fireemu had ignored it; a same-day change to store it was reverted and the regression now pins that it stays ignored.
gaps.nextAction: None; the revision 1 production record is published (auth-blocking-create-disable-r1) and fireemu keeps ignoring photoUrl at sign-up.

gaps.scope: Authentication versus authorization order on the end-user accounts:update route. Production (recorded and approved 2026-09-12, auth-refusal-precedence revision 1): a client accounts:update carrying a tampered ID token and an administrator-only field is refused INVALID_ID_TOKEN with nothing applied, so the session is verified before the administrator-only field is judged. fireemu refused OPERATION_NOT_ALLOWED, rejecting the field before verifying the session; it now verifies the session first on the end-user route. A valid session carrying such a field is still refused OPERATION_NOT_ALLOWED (local policy, unobserved for a valid token), the OOB route still rejects the field before consuming the code, and the localId selector is still refused.
gaps.nextAction: Closed for the recorded conditions: the production candidate and the local comparison on the corrected artifact (bound to commit c3a7973b, all nine rows agree) each carry a scoped approval, and regressions fence authenticate-before-authorize across expired, revoked, disabled and deleted sessions. Exact production precedence is established for the recorded tampered-signature case only; other invalid-token overlaps and a valid token with an administrator-only field remain unobserved (see AUTH-U13).
